# @zireal/result-kit

> Type-safe `Result` handling for TypeScript. A plain, method-less `Result` union,
> a data-first free-function core, and an opt-in fluent wrapper. Zero runtime
> dependencies, ESM-only, Node >=22.12, TypeScript >=6.0.

This file is a self-contained brief for coding agents. Read it and you can write
idiomatic `@zireal/result-kit` code without fetching anything else.
`llms-full.txt` is the long form (wire story, do-notation, recipes, migration).

**If you know `neverthrow`, read "Reflexes to unlearn" first — it is the section
that will save you.** Most of what an LLM produces for this package from prior
training is neverthrow-shaped and does not compile here.

---

## The union

```ts
type Result<T, E> = Ok<T> | Err<E>;

interface Ok<T>  { readonly ok: true;  readonly value: T }
interface Err<E> { readonly ok: false; readonly error: E }
```

**Plain data. No class, no methods, no brand.** Any `{ ok: true, value }` *is* an
`Ok<T>`, whoever built it. This is a deliberate guarantee, not an accident: it is
what lets a `Result` survive `JSON.stringify`, cross an HTTP boundary, and still
be a `Result` on the other side.

Consequences that matter when writing code:

- There is no `instanceof Result`. Use `isOk` / `isErr` / `isResult`.
- A `Result` has **exactly two fields** per half. Do not add a third.
- `.map()` on a plain `Result` does not exist. The core is free functions.

---

## Reflexes to unlearn

Left column is what an LLM reaches for by default (mostly `neverthrow`, some
`fp-ts` / Effect). Right column is what this package actually exports.

| Common reflex | Correct here | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `result.unwrapOr(0)` | `unwrapOr(result, 0)` | The core is **free functions**. Methods only exist on `/fluent` wrappers. |
| `result.map(f)` | `map(result, f)` | Same. Data-first, value as the first argument. |
| `result.match(okFn, errFn)` | `match(result, { ok, err })` | Ours takes **one object**, not two positional callbacks. |
| `Result.combine([a, b])` | `combine([a, b])` | No static namespace object. `combine` is a free function, and it is **tuple-preserving**. |
| `Result.combineWithAllErrors([…])` | `combineWithAllErrors([…])` | Same. |
| `result._unsafeUnwrap()` | `unwrapOrThrow(result)` | `_unsafeUnwrap` does not exist. `unwrapOrThrow` throws a real `Error` with the original in `cause`. |
| `result._unsafeUnwrapErr()` | `expectErr(result)` (tests) | No production equivalent — narrow with `isErr` instead. |
| `okAsync(v)` / `errAsync(e)` | *(no equivalent)* | Async is `Promise<Result>` in the core, or `ResultAsync.from(...)` on `/fluent`. |
| `ResultAsync.fromPromise(p, fn)` | `fromPromise(p, fn)` | A free function at the root, and also on `/fluent`. |
| `ResultAsync.fromSafePromise(p)` | *(no equivalent)* | Use `fromPromise` and supply the reject mapper. |
| `result.asyncMap(f)` / `.asyncAndThen(f)` | `.toAsync().map(f)` / `.toAsync().andThen(f)` | Crossing sync→async is **one explicit seam**, not per-method twins. |
| `Result.fromThrowable(fn, onErr)` | `fromThrowable(fn, onErr)` | Free function. |
| `fromAsyncThrowable(fn, onErr)` | `fromThrowableAsync(fn, onErr)` | Note the suffix position: `Async` goes **last**. |
| `yield* mightFail()` (neverthrow 8.1+) | `yield* safeUnwrap(mightFail())` | **The dangerous one.** neverthrow's `Result` became directly iterable in 8.1.0; ours is deliberately **not**, so this looks like it should work. `safeUnwrap` is a free function, root-only. |
| `yield* mightFail().safeUnwrap()` (≤8.0) | `yield* safeUnwrap(mightFail())` | Same target. Still present in neverthrow 8.x — deprecated in 8.1.1, slated for removal in 9.0.0. |
| `err._tag` / `err.code` / `err.kind` | `err.type` | The discriminant is `type`. Always. |
| `Data.TaggedError` / `extends Error` | `defineError('not_found', …)` | Typed errors are **plain objects**, never classes. |
| `Option` / `Maybe` / `Some` / `None` | *(not shipped)* | Deliberately out of scope. Use `toNullable` / `fromNullable`. |
| `import { ok } from '@zireal/result-kit/core'` | `from '@zireal/result-kit'` | There is no `/core` subpath. The root **is** the core. |

### The one that bites hardest

**`neverthrow`'s `.isOk()` narrows. `/fluent`'s `.isOk()` does not.**

```ts
// ✗ WRONG — chain.value does not exist, and this does not narrow
const chain = from(findUser(id));
if (chain.isOk()) chain.value;

// ✓ Leave the wrapper first, then narrow with the free-function guard
const result = from(findUser(id)).toResult();
if (isOk(result)) result.value;   // T

// ✓ Or never leave — collapse both branches
from(findUser(id)).match({ ok: (u) => u.name, err: () => 'anonymous' });
```

`/fluent`'s `.isOk()` / `.isErr()` return **plain booleans**. A method cannot emit
a type predicate about its own class's generics, so no narrowing is possible
there. The root's `isOk(r)` / `isErr(r)` *are* type predicates and do narrow.

---

## Root API — `@zireal/result-kit`

37 free functions. Import only what you use; the package is `sideEffects: false`
and genuinely tree-shakable.

**Constructors and guards**

```ts
ok(value)              // Ok<T>;  ok() with no args is Ok<void>
err(error)             // Err<E> — the single generic failure constructor
isOk(r) / isErr(r)     // type predicates — these narrow
isTypedError(e)        // does this value follow the TypedError convention?
defineError(type, msg) // build a typed-error constructor
defineError.withData<D>()(type, msg)  // …when the payload pairs with a STATIC message
defineErrors(registry) // group constructors so ErrorsOf derives the union
isResult(v)            // is this unknown a Result? (type predicate)
parseResult(v)         // the same check, returning a typed error saying why not
```

**Transforms** — each accepts a `Result` *or* a `Promise<Result>`

```ts
map(r, fn)             // transform the value; Err passes through
mapErr(r, fn)          // transform the error; Ok passes through
andThen(r, fn)         // chain a fallible step; error channel widens to E | F
orElse(r, fn)          // recover from an error
inspect(r, fn)         // tee the Ok side for a side effect; returns r unchanged
inspectErr(r, fn)      // tee the Err side
```

**Terminals** — these leave the `Result` world

```ts
match(r, { ok, err })  // collapse both branches; exhaustive by construction
unwrapOr(r, fallback)
unwrapOrElse(r, fn)    // fallback computed from the error
unwrapOrThrow(r, msg?) // the value, or THROW a real Error (original in `cause`)
toNullable(r)          // the value, or null
```

**Collections**

```ts
combine(results)               // all-or-nothing; preserves the TUPLE type; first Err wins
combineWithAllErrors(results)  // same, but collects EVERY error into an array
partition(results)             // [values, errors] — both halves, always
```

Both combinators also take a **record**, and return one keyed identically —
`partition` does not. The record form of `combineWithAllErrors` accumulates
`KeyedError<K, E>` entries (`{ key, error }`) instead of a flat array, so you can
tell which field failed; the array form stays flat.

```ts
combine({ user: findUser(id), posts: listPosts(id) });
// Result<{ user: User; posts: Post[] }, NotFound | Timeout>

const checked = combineWithAllErrors({ name: checkName(i), age: checkAge(i) });
// Err carries (KeyedError<'name', NameError> | KeyedError<'age', AgeError>)[]
if (!checked.ok) prettifyErrors(checked.error.map((e) => e.error)); // BRIDGE: unwrap first
```

`groupByType` and `prettifyErrors` take a flat `TypedError[]`, so a `KeyedError[]`
must be mapped through `(e) => e.error` first. "First Err" over a record means
**property order** (`Object.keys`: integer-like keys ascending, then insertion
order), own enumerable keys only; symbol keys are silently invisible.
`combine({})` is `ok({})`. An entry that is not a `Result` — a present-but-
`undefined` optional key, or a hole in a sparse array — throws a named
diagnostic rather than a bare `TypeError`.

**Error matching and formatting**

```ts
matchType(error, arms)            // one arm per variant; a missing arm is a COMPILE ERROR
matchType(error, arms, fallback)  // partial arms; fallback sees only the RESIDUAL variants
groupByType(errors)               // TypedError[] -> partial record keyed by `type`
prettifyErrors(errors)            // TypedError[] -> one "✖ type: message" line each
```

**Interop — ways into the `Result` world**

```ts
fromNullable(value, error)        // null/undefined becomes an Err
fromPredicate(value, pred, error) // narrows T when pred is a type guard
fromThrowable(fn, onThrow)        // wrap a throwing fn into a Result-returning one
fromPromise(promise, onReject)    // catch a REJECTION into the error channel
fromThrowableAsync(fn, onReject)  // the lazy, reusable form of fromPromise
fromSchema(schema, options?)      // any Standard Schema validator -> Result-returning fn
fromSchemaAsync(schema, options?) // the same, for asynchronous validation
```

**Do-notation**

```ts
safeTry(function* () { … })       // run a generator; any Err short-circuits the block
safeUnwrap(r)                     // makes a plain Result yield*-able. ROOT ONLY.
```

**Test assertions** — they assert a branch, then **extract** (matchers cannot do the second)

```ts
expectOk(r)   // the value, or throw a descriptive error
expectErr(r)  // the error, or throw
```

**Types** — `Result` `Ok` `Err` `TypedError` `ErrorCtor` `ErrorsOf` `OkTypeOf`
`ErrTypeOf` `ValidationIssue` `ValidationFailed` `FromSchemaOptions`
`MalformedResult` `MalformedResultReason` `KeyedError`

---

## Producing a `Result`

```ts
import { ok, err } from '@zireal/result-kit';
import type { Result } from '@zireal/result-kit';

function findUser(id: string): Result<User, NotFound> {
  const user = db.get(id);

  return user ? ok(user) : err({ type: 'not_found', message: `No user ${id}` });
}
```

Annotate the return type. Inference works, but the annotation is what makes the
error channel a stable, documented contract rather than whatever fell out.

---

## Typed errors

`E` is fully generic — a `Result`'s error may be a string, an `Error`, anything.
`TypedError` is an **opt-in** convention for errors you want to narrow on:

```ts
{ type: string; message: string; details?: TData; cause?: unknown }
```

Plain objects. **Never classes, never `extends Error`.** They serialize, and they
narrow.

```ts
import { defineError, defineErrors, err } from '@zireal/result-kit';
import type { ErrorsOf } from '@zireal/result-kit';

const notFound = defineError('not_found', (d: { id: string }) => `No user ${d.id}`);
const forbidden = defineError('forbidden', 'Not permitted');

export const appErrors = defineErrors({ notFound, forbidden });
export type AppError = ErrorsOf<typeof appErrors>;
//          ^? TypedError<'not_found', { id: string }> | TypedError<'forbidden', never>

err(notFound({ id: 'u1' }));   // Err<TypedError<'not_found', { id: string }>>
```

Each constructor also carries `.type` (readable without building a value) and a
`.is()` runtime guard.

**`defineError`'s second argument is a string (a fixed message) *or* a function
of the payload (a computed one).** A payload paired with a **static** message is
the one shape that form cannot infer, and getting it wrong fails *silently*:

```ts
// ✗ TYPECHECKS, then silently drops `details` at runtime. Nothing is declared
//   for the constructor to read, so it builds a no-payload variant.
defineError<'conflict', { id: string }>('conflict', 'Already exists');

// ✓ The escape hatch — supplies the payload type without repeating the tag.
defineError.withData<{ id: string }>()('conflict', 'Already exists');
```

Use the single-call form whenever the message is computed from the payload;
reach for `.withData` only for the static-message-plus-payload case.

### Dispatching on the error

```ts
import { match, matchType } from '@zireal/result-kit';

const status = matchType(error, {
  not_found: () => 404,
  forbidden: () => 403,
  conflict: (e) => (e.details!.slug ? 409 : 400),
});
//    ^? number — the union of every arm's return type
```

A catch-all is the **third parameter**, never a `_` key in the arm bag — only that
position narrows to the *residual* (unhandled) variants:

```ts
matchType(error, { not_found: () => 404 }, (e) => {
  //                                        ^? forbidden | conflict
  return 500;
});
```

Coming from a `Result`, compose the two:

```ts
match(result, {
  ok: () => 200,
  err: (e) => matchType(e, { not_found: () => 404, forbidden: () => 403 }),
});
```

---

## The two surfaces

Both are first-class. Pick per project, or mix per file.

```ts
// free-function core — libraries, hot paths, minimal bundles. Reads inside-out.
import { map, mapErr, unwrapOr } from '@zireal/result-kit';
const label = unwrapOr(mapErr(map(r, (u) => u.name), (e) => e.message), 'anon');

// /fluent — application code, linear pipelines. Reads left-to-right.
import { from } from '@zireal/result-kit/fluent';
const label = from(r).map((u) => u.name).mapErr((e) => e.message).unwrapOr('anon');
```

**Default to `/fluent` for application code.** The core never needs `/fluent` —
that self-sufficiency is the point of the split.

The plain union is **the source of truth**. A wrapper is a transient envelope for
the duration of a chain: never store it, never serialize it, never return it
across a boundary. Leave with `.toResult()`.

### Async

```ts
import { ResultAsync } from '@zireal/result-kit/fluent';

const name = await ResultAsync.from(loadUser(id))
  .andThen(requireActive)
  .map((user) => user.name)
  .match({ ok: (n) => n, err: () => 'anonymous' });
```

`ResultAsync` implements `PromiseLike`, so `await` collapses it to the plain
`Result` — awaiting *is* the sanctioned way out.

Sync→async is **one explicit seam**, `.toAsync()`:

```ts
import { ok } from '@zireal/result-kit/fluent';   // the WRAPPER ok, not the root's

ok(user).map(validate).toAsync().andThen(saveRemote);
```

Explicit on purpose: a settled `Result` cannot promise an asynchronous output,
because a transform that short-circuits never runs its callback at all — on the
`Err` branch there would be nothing to await.

In the **core**, async is just `Promise<Result<T, E>>`. No new type, no `Async`
twin of anything — transforms accept a value or a promise in the same signature.

---

## Do-notation

For flows where chaining gets awkward: branches, early exits, a step needing a
value from two steps back. Any `Err` exits the whole block.

```ts
import { ok, safeTry, safeUnwrap } from '@zireal/result-kit';

const total = safeTry(function* () {
  const user = yield* safeUnwrap(findUser(id));      // an Err here short-circuits
  const order = yield* safeUnwrap(loadOrder(user));  // each binds its own type

  return ok(user.credit + order.total);              // return a Result EXPLICITLY
});
//    ^? Result<number, NotFound | OrderMissing>  — the error channel accumulates
```

Two rules the generator body must follow:

1. **`return ok(v)`, never a bare `v`.** The body returns a `Result`.
2. On `/fluent` there is **no `safeUnwrap`** — the wrappers are self-iterable, so
   `yield* from(findUser(id))` directly, and the block hands back a wrapper.

Async is the same runner with an `async function*`; there is no `safeTryAsync`.

---

## Gotchas

**1. A discriminated-union return widens inside `safeTry`.**

```ts
return ok({ kind: 'noop' });                        // ✗ kind widens to string
return ok({ kind: 'noop' } satisfies MyUnion);      // ✓ pin the literal
```

The generator's return type is inferred *before* it is checked against your
union. `as const` or `ok<MyUnion>({ … })` also work.

**2. `details` stays optional after the tag narrows.** Narrowing `type` does not
make the payload non-optional — arms read `e.details!.id` or `e.details?.id`.
That is a `TypedError` fact, not a `matchType` one.

**3. Only a *closed* union can be exhausted.** A bare `TypedError` has an open
`string` tag, so *any* set of arms satisfies it. Exhaustiveness needs a union of
specific variants — what `ErrorsOf` gives you.

**4. `ok()` with no argument round-trips to a one-field object.** The value is
`{ ok: true, value: undefined }`, but `JSON.stringify` omits an `undefined`
property, so `{ ok: true }` arrives with the `value` **key gone**. `parseResult`
accepts that deliberately; code doing `'value' in revived` on the round-tripped
object will be surprised. (`parseResult`'s own envelope is a different thing —
its `.value` is the inner `Result`, always present.)

**5. `cause` is the one field that breaks serialization.** It is typed `unknown`,
so it is the one route a non-serializable value takes into an otherwise JSON-safe
`Result`. Strip it at the boundary. This collides directly with `fromSchema`'s
`{ includeCause: true }`, which puts the **raw vendor issues** — the rejected
input included — there.

**6. `unwrapOrThrow` is a v1 name that changed meaning.** Both versions throw —
what changed is *what*. v1's `/nest` `unwrapOrThrow` threw a NestJS
`HttpException`; the 5.x core one throws a plain `Error` with the original in
`cause`. So a handled `404` becomes an unhandled `500` under Nest's default
filter. It survives find-and-replace and still typechecks: this is the
migration's **only silent breakage**.

**7. ESM only.** No CJS build. `moduleResolution` must be `"bundler"`,
`"node16"`, or `"nodenext"`.

---

## Across the wire

A `Result` is plain data by contract, so it crosses a process boundary intact and
**stays a `Result`**. That is the package's central claim: end-to-end typed
errors, server to client, with no codegen step.

**When the type crosses with the value** (server action, typed RPC, tRPC, a typed
worker channel) — there is nothing to do. The client already has
`Result<Booking, BookingError>` and narrows it directly.

**When the type is lost** (`fetch`, `postMessage`, a queue) — `response.json()`
hands you `unknown`. Do **not** close that with `as Result<T, E>`. Prove it in two
steps:

```ts
const envelope = parseResult(await response.json());
if (isErr(envelope)) return `Bad response (${envelope.error.details?.reason})`;

const result = envelope.value;                 // Result<unknown, unknown> — envelope proven
if (isErr(result)) return renderError(result.error);

const booking = parseBooking(result.value);    // fromSchema — payload proven
```

`parseResult` proves the **envelope** and takes no generic on purpose;
`fromSchema` proves the **payload**. The envelope is provable and its cargo is
not, so they stay separate steps.

---

## Validation — `fromSchema`

Zod 4, Valibot, ArkType and Effect Schema all implement Standard Schema v1, a
**types-only** spec — so one adapter covers all of them with no dependency added.

```ts
const parseUser = fromSchema(UserSchema);   // wrap once, call many times
const result = parseUser(await req.json()); // Result<User, ValidationFailed>
```

The error is a **single** `TypedError<'validation_failed', { issues }>` — one
error channel, one error — so it composes with `matchType`, `groupByType` and
`combineWithAllErrors` like any other typed error.

Each issue keeps only the two fields Standard Schema *guarantees*: `message`, and
`path` normalized to an array (`[]` means the root). Vendor extras — Zod's
`code`, `expected`, `input` — are **dropped**, which is what keeps `details`
identical across vendors and provably JSON-safe. The price: you cannot branch on
*what kind* of failure occurred.

`fromSchema` is synchronous and **throws** if handed an async schema. Use
`fromSchemaAsync` when you do not know statically which you have.

---

## Testing

A `Result` is plain data, so assert structurally — no custom matcher needed:

```ts
expect(await changePlan(input)).toEqual(ok({ kind: 'noop' }));
```

To read `.value` after asserting the branch, use the extracting assertions —
they throw on the wrong branch and **return** the payload:

```ts
import { expectOk, expectErr } from '@zireal/result-kit';

const value = expectOk(await loadPlan(id));
const error = expectErr(await failingCall());
```

Optional Vitest matchers live at `@zireal/result-kit/testing`. Register them
explicitly — importing does **not** register them:

```ts
import { expect } from 'vitest';
import { resultMatchers } from '@zireal/result-kit/testing';

expect.extend(resultMatchers);
```

`toBeOk` / `toBeOkWith` / `toBeErr` / `toBeErrWith`. Both `*With` forms are deep
equality; partial matching is Vitest's own `expect.objectContaining`. The
matchers **assert but do not narrow** — keep `expectOk` / `expectErr` for
reading the value.

---

## Entrypoints

| Specifier | Contents |
|---|---|
| `@zireal/result-kit` | The free-function core. 37 functions, flat barrel. |
| `@zireal/result-kit/fluent` | `ok` `err` `from` `safeTry` `fromPromise` `fromThrowableAsync` `ResultAsync`, plus the `ResultChain` type. |
| `@zireal/result-kit/testing` | `resultMatchers` — the four Vitest matchers. |

There is no `/core`, no `/fp-ts`, no `/nest`. Those were v1 entrypoints and are
gone.

**Array-shaped helpers stay root-only** — `combine`, `combineWithAllErrors`,
`partition`, `fromNullable`, `fromPredicate`, `fromThrowable`. They take arrays or
non-`Result` inputs, so there is no instance for a method to hang off. Re-enter
the wrapper with `from(...)`:

```ts
from(combine([a, b])).map(sum).unwrapOr(0);
```

---

## Naming

Use these words; avoid the alternatives.

| Use | Not |
|---|---|
| `Result` | Either, Outcome |
| `Ok` / `Err` | Success / Failure (v1 names) |
| `ok` / `err` | success / failure / fail (v1 names) |
| `isOk` / `isErr` | isSuccess / isFailure |
| `TypedError` | TaggedError, AppError, DomainError |
| `type` (the discriminant) | tag, `_tag`, kind, code |
| `details` | data, payload, meta, context |
| `defineError` | makeError, createError |
| `ResultChain` / `ResultAsync` | ResultPipeline, AsyncResult, TaskResult (v1 / genre names) |
| `safeTry` | gen, doNotation, attempt, tryCatch, safeTryAsync |
| `safeUnwrap` | unwrap (means "throws" across the genre — deliberately unused) |
| `matchType` | matchError, matchTag, exhaustive |

---

Full documentation: <https://github.com/alifaroo-q/result-kit>
